## Shared vocabulary

| Term | IRI | Definition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `StaffId` | https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/division-ontology#StaffId | The enterprise-wide staff number issued by the HR system and used as the internal primary key by older enterprise systems. Exactly 7 characters: U or N followed by 6 digits, case-insensitive and normalised to uppercase. Unique per member of staff, never reissued and never changed. The identity provider is its source of truth; applications read it from a token claim and do not edit it. |

Candidate and appointment details contain identifiers, canonical codes, and old/new statuses only, never names, email addresses, clinical data, or arbitrary free text. |  |

Admin is exclusive and unscoped; Coordinator may combine with Manager and/or AppointmentStaff; Manager and AppointmentStaff share one `AppointmentType` scope, which may briefly be null immediately after a scoped role is synced and before an Admin assigns it — that transitional shape grants no capabilities. Absence of a profile means the authenticated identity is unassigned. |  |

Every staff-facing handler requests one of these rather than checking `Role` directly, so a newly added role gains only the capabilities its role mapping grants. |  |

Exactly 7 characters: `U` or `N` followed by 6 digits, case-insensitive — always normalised to uppercase, so two values differing only in case are the same `StaffId`. Unique per member of staff, never reissued and never changed, which is what makes it safe for JointBooking to mirror. The identity provider is its source of truth; JointBooking only ever reads it from a token claim and never edits it. | exact: https://github.com/jamiemitchellconsultants/division-ontology#StaffId |
| `StaffIdentity` | https://jointbooking.internal/ontology#StaffIdentity | The application's mirror of one authenticated staff identity: the provider-assigned `staffUserId` paired with the `StaffId` that identity's token carries, learned from the token itself. It exists so an Admin can address a colleague by `StaffId` instead of by opaque identifier, and so `StaffId` can be shown wherever a staff identity is displayed. `displayName` is the same idea applied to a human-readable name rather than the staff number, mirrored from the token's own name claim when the identity provider is configured to emit one; it is null when no such claim has ever been observed for that identity. It is a cache of identity-provider-owned data and is never the source of truth for any field. A row appears the first time an identity calls the API, which may be before any `StaffAccessProfile` assigns it a role. |  |

Not reachable through any Admin-facing route. |  |

## Rules and invariants

| Source | Concept | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `StaffAccessProfile` | Admin is exclusive and has no `AppointmentType`; Coordinator may combine with Manager and/or AppointmentStaff but never Admin; Manager and AppointmentStaff share the profile's one `AppointmentType` scope. Admin receives no candidate data. Each `AppointmentType` has at most one current Manager profile, while any number of AppointmentStaff profiles may share it. Manager or AppointmentStaff may transiently carry a null scope immediately after an identity-provider role sync and before an Admin assigns the appointment type; that shape is valid but grants no capabilities until scope is set. See [Issue #71 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-scoped-multi-role-authorization-design.md) and [IdP-sourced roles design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-idp-sourced-staff-roles-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `CandidateReadiness` | `Ready` requires an active original Booking and one Completed Booking Appointment for every current derived Candidate Requirement across that original Booking and its non-cancelled recovery Bookings. Expected, Checked in, and No-show are outstanding; cancelled Booking Appointments and non-required Appointment Types are excluded. No active original Booking, a temporarily unassigned Employee Group, or a requirement snapshot mismatch is explicitly not ready. See [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | Recovery Booking | A recovery Invite and Booking cover only current requirements whose latest non-cancelled Booking Appointment is No-show and for which no Completed attempt exists. Completed appointments are never recreated or charged capacity again. A recovery Booking becomes Concluded when all its appointments are Completed or No-show; repeated No-show can then create another recovery. A No-show correction is rejected while a later pending or non-cancelled recovery exists. See [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `SlotWindow` | Every window is exactly 4 hours; only its `date` and `startTime` are stored, so a proposal and the `ConfirmedSlot` derived from it can never disagree about duration. See [Plan 02](detailed-implementations/2026-09-03-joint-booking/02-domain-appointment-types.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `StaffIdentity` | Exactly one row per authenticated staff identity, keyed by `staffUserId`, with `staffId` unique across the table. Both fields are immutable in practice: the provider never reissues `staffUserId` for the same person and HR never changes a `StaffId`. An authenticated request whose pair is not already cached upserts it, so the mirror converges from tokens alone, without a directory query; `lastSeenAt` is refreshed on those writes only and is therefore approximate. `displayName` refreshes on the same cache-miss cadence as `lastSeenAt` and carries the same approximateness — it can lag a rename in the identity provider until the next sign-in — and, unlike `staffId`, its absence never blocks anything: a null `displayName` falls back to `staffId` or an opaque identifier wherever a staff identity is shown. A token with no `StaffId` claim, or one carrying a malformed value, records no row and is refused by every staff-authorized endpoint even where a `StaffAccessProfile` exists, since a staff identity JointBooking cannot name must not appear in an `AuditLog`. See [StaffId claim design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-staff-id-claim-design.md) and [Staff identity display name design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-15-staff-identity-display-name-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `ConfirmedSlot` | A `SlotProposal` becomes a `ConfirmedSlot` only once all 3 Managers (one per `AppointmentType`) have accepted it, each supplying their own headcount. An Admin or Coordinator may instead bulk-import a `ConfirmedSlot` directly, with `proposalId` left null; either way, once created it behaves identically for every later operation. See [Area B](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/b-slot-negotiation.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `ProposalAcceptance` | While its `SlotProposal` remains `Open`, the manager recorded in `managerUserId` may replace their own positive `headcount` without withdrawing the acceptance. A different manager cannot read or change that value. See [Area B](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/b-slot-negotiation.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `SlotCapacity` | `remainingCapacity` must never go below 0 or above the current `totalHeadcount` for that `AppointmentType` on that `ConfirmedSlot`. While the slot remains `Active`, its current Manager may replace `totalHeadcount` with a positive total no lower than the active-booking count, changing `remainingCapacity` by the same delta. Every read-check-write is one atomic, row-locked transaction. This is the mechanism behind "no overbooking." See [Area G](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/g-capacity-concurrency-rules.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `Invite` | Every `Invite` offers exactly 3 `InviteOption`s, each a `ConfirmedSlot` with spare `SlotCapacity` in every snapshotted `InviteRequirement`. An initial Invite snapshots every current derived `CandidateRequirement`; a recovery Invite snapshots only recoverable outstanding no-show types and identifies the active original Booking. A group-changing edit supersedes a pending initial Invite, while a Coordinator may explicitly cancel a recovery Invite. See [Area D](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/d-invite-engine.md) and [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `Booking` | Cancelling a `ConfirmedSlot` voids every `Booking` against it, frees its `SlotCapacity`, and triggers a fresh `Invite` for each affected `Candidate`. See [Area F](superpowers/plans/2026-09-03-joint-booking/f-cancellation-reschedule.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `BookingAppointment` | A booking creates exactly one per candidate requirement in the same transaction, unique by (`Booking`, `AppointmentType`). Its normal lifecycle is `Expected` → `CheckedIn` → `Completed` or `Expected` → `NoShow`; only the bounded corrections `CheckedIn` → `Expected`, `Completed` → `CheckedIn`, and `NoShow` → `Expected` are permitted. A same-status submission is idempotent. Check-in is limited to the slot's head-office date, no-show is permitted only after its four-hour window, and every real transition is versioned and audited. Active bookings and active slots are required for mutation. See [Issue #26 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-booking-appointment-workspace-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `CandidateRequirement` | The requirement set cannot change while the candidate has an active original `Booking`; name and email corrections and set-equivalent Employee Group changes remain permitted. Outside a legacy reconciliation window, requirements are derived only from the Candidate's active `EmployeeGroup` and are never caller-selected. Cancellation makes old `BookingAppointment` records read-only and a replacement initial booking snapshots the then-current set. See [Issue #26 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-07-booking-appointment-workspace-design.md) and [Issue #91 design](superpowers/specs/2026-09-09-employee-group-requirements-design.md). |
| jamiemitchellconsultants/JointBooking | `EmployeeGroup` | The initial five groups and their mappings to the existing three fixed Appointment Types are deterministic, change-controlled reference data.
